text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for seeing this six-year-old boy for further evaluation of longstanding visual difficulties that were first noted during early infancy. He was born at full term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, is currently meeting all his general educational and developmental milestones, and takes no daily medications. There is no family history of early-onset ocular disorders.

On examination, he demonstrates a marked reduction in visual acuity, fixing and following inconsistently with each eye. Ocular alignment demonstrates a distinct outward drift consistent with an alternating exotropia, alongside persistent, fine rhythmic conjugate oscillations in keeping with nystagmus. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals that both crystalline lenses are heavily attenuated and flattened, appearing as dense membranous sheets rather than formed structures. Importantly, the lenses are entirely devoid of any dust-like or pulverulent opacities. 

A-scan biometry was completed and confirmed that the axial length of both globes remains thoroughly normal for his age group, with no evidence of ocular elongation. His corneas are clear, intraocular pressures are well controlled, and the visible portions of the posterior segment appear unremarkable.

I would appreciate your comprehensive pediatric ophthalmic assessment and recommendations regarding ongoing visual rehabilitation and potential operative strategies.

Sincerely,

Dr. Evelyn Vance
